key: Then Moses said unto Aaron: ‘This is it that the LORD spoke, saying: Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified, and before all the people I will be glorified.’ And Aaron held his peace.
s: When fire from the LORD consumes Nadab and Abihu after their strange fire, Moses speaks to their father; Rashi, on 10:3, hears Moses telling Aaron he had expected the sanctuary to be hallowed through himself or Aaron and now sees the sons as greater, and Rashbam, on 10:3, as a charge not to mourn or leave the service.
src: Rashi (Rosenbaum and Silbermann Hebrew, 1929 to 1934) and Rashbam (Hebrew, Daat edition), on Leviticus 10:3, Sefaria export commit 3f10136 (2026)

evidence.gloss: [Rashi on 10:3, ‘this is it that the LORD spoke’:] Moses said to Aaron: Aaron my brother, I knew that the House would be hallowed through those intimate with the Omnipresent, and I thought it would be either through me or through you; now I see that they are greater than I and than you … [Rashbam on 10:3, ‘then Moses said unto Aaron’:] Do not mourn, do not weep, and do not cease from the service, for this thing that I tell you is what the LORD spoke: through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok; ref Leviticus 10:3 and at [99,3] match). Plain sense faithful: 10:1 to 10:2 Nadab and Abihu offer strange fire and fire from before the LORD devours them; 10:3 Moses speaks to Aaron. Opened the whole 10:3 packet (Rashi, Ibn Ezra, Ramban, Rashbam, Sforno, Leviticus Rabbah 20:4 and the pointer to 12:2). Rashi on 10:3 gives, from the Sifra, Moses telling Aaron he knew the House would be hallowed through those near to God, had thought it would be through himself or Aaron, and now sees the sons are greater: the reading is his. But the proposal labelled Rashi’s reading ‘consolation’: that word is not in Rashi’s comment; it is Rashbam’s description of the aggadah he rejects. CHANGED the Rashi clause to what Rashi’s words carry (Moses telling Aaron he had expected the sanctuary to be hallowed through himself or Aaron and now sees the sons as greater) and the verb to ‘hears’; the sentence is now 58 words. Rashbam on 10:3 says in his own words: do not mourn, do not weep, do not cease from the service, and he calls the consolation aggadah not the plain sense: the two genuinely differ (rule 5), named without resolving. Key, ref, at, src unchanged. Evidence pieces machine-matched against the packet. entry-check ok.
